title: Breaking the cubic barrier for the inverse-free Solovay-Kitaev algorithm
summary: The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm states that it is possible to efficiently compile unitaries to accuracy $ε$ in $\text{polylog}(1/ε)$ time using any universal gate set. While Solovay and Kitaev's initial work addressed inverse-closed gate sets, recently Bouland and Giurgicǎ-Tiron showed it is possible to efficiently compile arbitrary gate sets without inverses. However, the exponent of their compilation algorithm is high. For example the inverse-free exponent for a qubit is over $8.62$, while information theoretically it is known that an inverse-free exponent of $3$ is possible in any dimension…
